title: Launch microcard visual kit — modular feature-callout and before/after UI assets (accessibility variants)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Produce a compact, reusable microcard image kit for the product changelog and announcement blog that covers feature callouts, before/after UI comparisons, and accessibility-ready variants. Deliver a single source Figma file and exported asset pack for engineering, marketing, and docs.

Scope and constraints: create modular templates that can be repurposed for multiple release posts (small edits only). Each microcard must have: a feature callout overlay, before/after split or side-by-side layout, dark and light themes, mobile (360x640) and social-ready hero crops (1200x628 and 800x800), and an accessible color palette that meets AA contrast for text overlays. Include alt-text examples and short caption copy for each variant.

Deliverables:
- Figma source file with component library and named variants (microcard/feature-callout, microcard/before-after, microcard/thumbnail).
- Exported asset zip with PNG/JPEG/WebP at specified sizes and 2x retina assets.
- Layered PSD and SVG exports for partner teams that require edits.
- Documentation doc in Drive with naming conventions, export checklist, color tokens, and alt-text templates.
- One example assembled for the upcoming console-2025.03 release (hero + three supporting microcards).

Acceptance criteria: all exported hero images pass visual QA, copy fits within defined safe area, color contrast verified, assets named and versioned according to the release tag, and marketing/PM sign-off on final set.

Design trade-offs considered: tight aspect ratios for social crops may require slight UI cropping; chosen approach prioritizes preserving key UI elements within defined safe zones rather than full-width captures. For complex interactive screens we will use annotated static snapshots rather than animated GIFs to reduce file size and ensure consistency across channels.
comments: 2025-02-14 Aisha Patel: Scoped initial deliverables with PM. Agreed on component-first approach and export sizes. Asked ENG for guidance on in-app screenshot safe areas.

2025-02-18 Miguel Santos: Drafted Figma components and basic tokens. Pushed two pattern directions (overlay left vs overlay right). Calling out potential overlap with existing branding palette — suggested we add an accessible accent set.

2025-02-21 Kendall Morris (PM): Reviewed initial directions. Prefers overlay-left for hero but asked for a compact micro variant for list pages. Requested alt-text templates for each microcard and one internationalized caption example.

2025-02-24 Engineering note (Priya Rao): Confirmed safe crop margins for embedded docs are 48px on small widths. Flagged that telemetry dashboard widgets have dynamic elements that should be blurred in screenshots for stable visuals.
2025-02-27 Design review: Iterated on color contrast. Added high-contrast text variant and a nondestructive shadow option to improve legibility on busy screenshots. Running export QA next week.
2025-03-02 Marketing feedback (Lena Cho): Social thumbnail feels tight at 800x800; asked for a 1:1 center-crop variant that preserves CTA area. Also requested WebP exports for site load performance.
2025-03-03 Miguel Santos: Updated Figma with final naming conventions and uploaded export zip to Drive. Pending PM sign-off and marketing assets approval before closing.
Next steps: run visual QA checklist, produce layered PSDs, finalize Drive doc, add to release PR checklist.
